title: Estimation and Inference for Peer Effects under Conditional Random Assignment
abstract: arXiv:2608.16468v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Empirical studies of peer effects often exploit conditional random assignment to peer groups within urns. We develop a GMM framework for estimation and inference in this setting. The framework separately identifies endogenous and contextual peer effects and nests tests of random peer-group assignment as a special case. It permits unknown heteroskedasticity and corrects finite-urn bias in variance estimation. Its asymptotic theory allows the number of peer groups to grow through more urns, more groups within urns, or both. We establish the asymptotic validity of the procedures and evaluate their finite-sample performance through Monte Carlo simulations. We apply the method to study peer effects on personality among university students. For traits with positive reduced-form peer effects, the estimates indicate that positive contextual effects are partly offset by negative endogenous effects.

translated_title: 条件随机分配下同伴效应的估计与推断
translated_abstract: 同伴效应的实证研究常利用瓮内条件随机分配至同伴群体的方法。我们在此背景下开发了一个广义矩估计（GMM）框架，用于估计与推断。该框架分别识别内生性同伴效应和情境性同伴效应，并将随机同伴群体分配的检验作为特例嵌套其中。它允许未知异方差性，并修正了有限瓮方差估计中的偏差。其渐近理论允许同伴群体数量通过更多瓮、瓮内更多群体或两者同时增加而增长。我们建立了这些程序的有效性，并通过蒙特卡洛模拟评估了它们的有限样本性能。我们将该方法应用于研究大学生个性中的同伴效应。对于具有正简化形式同伴效应的特质，估计表明正情境效应部分被负内生效应所抵消。
tldr: 本文提出了一种GMM框架，用于在条件随机分配下分别估计同伴效应中的内生和情境效应，并应用于大学生个性研究发现正情境效应被负内生效应部分抵消。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a GMM framework to separately estimate endogenous and contextual peer effects under conditional random assignment, and applying it to university students' personality reveals that positive contextual effects are partly offset by negative endogenous effects.
